# Le049 — Carriage-return stripping during STEP file write

## Description

A STEP writer normalises line endings by stripping all `\r` characters. When a string literal contains a literal carriage return (e.g., a multi-line description in a `DESCRIPTION` field), the stripping also applies inside string contexts — corrupting embedded text.

## Reproducer recipe

STEP record `DESCRIPTION_ATTRIBUTE('line1\r\nline2','desc')` where the `\r` is intentional. Writer strips, output reads `line1\nline2`.

## Expected kernel behavior

line-ending normalisation only outside string literals; preserve string contents byte-for-byte (with proper escaping via `\X\` if needed).

## Notes

**See also**: Le017, Le028. Provenance tier: requires-sibling-pair — bytes alone cannot demonstrate the writer-side stripping; the defect is the differential between the writer's input (string containing `\r`) and its output (string without `\r`). Demonstrating this requires both an input fixture and the corrupted output it produces, exercised through a STEP writer.
